messages:
alex_support: hi team, escalating a live customer issue — Acme is hitting an MFA loop after their session expires. customer reports: they sign back in with SSO, go through MFA, then immediately redirected to login again.

alex_support: repro steps i got from them: open app, idle >30m, try to use endpoint -> 401 redirect to SSO. after SSO finishes they land back on /auth/callback then redirect to /login with no error shown. tried in chrome and safari.

alex_support: included headers from failed callback (redacted customer):
```
POST /auth/callback HTTP/1.1
Host: app.acme.example
Cookie: session=eyJhbGciOi...; device_trust=1; __Host-session=...
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
```
Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: /login
Set-Cookie: session=; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=Lax
```
They also pasted browser console: blocked cookie due to SameSite attribute on cross-site redirect.

alex_support: tagging infra/sso since looks like cookie attr change might be involved. @julia_sre can you take a look? :eyes:

julia_sre: on it. timeline? customer is in prod and blocked now?

alex_support: yes, they just hit it. critical-severity; they can't complete auth flows.

ida_idp: i pulled the idp logs for session id they gave (redacted) — seeing token exchange succeed at idp, then our callback handler rejects with 400 "missing azp claim" in token validation step. that's odd, azp should be present for OIDC web flows.

ida_idp: also seeing repeated attempts from same browser while idp responds OK. looks like the browser isn't sending the __Host-session cookie back on callback POST (sameSite behavior). our handler then assumes no active session and issues a fresh redirect to /login.

julia_sre: any recent deploys that touched cookie config or callback endpoints? fetch deploy history.

deploy-bot: deploys:
- 1742098800 - webapp v2.14.1 (cookie refactor) by @sam_security
- 1742080000 - idp service 1.3.8 by @ida_idp

sam_security: i made the cookie refactor to set SameSite=Lax by default to harden CSRF, but i left a note that cross-site callback for legacy SSO clients needed SameSite=None. i thought idp had a compatibility shim.

sam_security: tagging @ida_idp — can we confirm whether idp shim is present and active?

ida_idp: checking idp 1.3.8 config — we missed the compatibility flag for legacy flows due to a config prune. by default library now sets device_trust cookie with SameSite=Lax, which breaks POST callback from third-party idp identity provider that uses cross-site POST.

ida_idp: reproduction steps i used locally:
1) start ngrok to simulate external idp
2) run curl that mimics idp POST with redirect:
```
curl -i -X POST 'https://app.local/auth/callback' \
  -H "Cookie: device_trust=1; __Host-session=abc123" \
  -d 'id_token=...&state=...'
```
Result: 302 -> /login and Set-Cookie clearing session. header shows cookie not honored by browser simulation because SameSite mismatch.

julia_sre: ok root cause is cookie SameSite change. immediate mitigation steps?

ida_idp: short-term: revert cookie policy for callback-relevant cookies to SameSite=None; Secure; HttpOnly for now. that will allow the idp POST to carry the device_trust/session cookie. we'll need to coordinate a safe rollout and update cookie doc.

sam_security: i'll push a hotfix to webapp to set SameSite=None for __Host-session and device_trust for callback endpoints only. will also add a feature-flag gated rollout.

julia_sre: runbook for support: advise affected customers to clear browser cookies and try incognito as immediate workaround. also ask them to accept device trust prompt if present. share this note with Acme.

alex_support: outreach drafted, will send immediate steps to Acme (clear cookies / incognito / reauth) and let them know we're patching.

ida_idp: longer-term: add a compatibility test in CI that simulates cross-site idp POSTs and asserts session cookie is accepted. also update cookie security docs to call out callbacks.

sam_security: timeline: hotfix PR in next 30m, canary deploy to staging in 45m, prod rollback/patch in 2hrs depending on approvals.

julia_sre: assign incident ticket INC-2026-045 to track. @sam_security make sure you include an audit of any other cookies that were tightened in the refactor.

sam_security: will do. also adding a note: some older browsers will still block SameSite=None unless Secure is set — ensure we include Secure attr.

ida_idp: QA notes: when you test, watch for logs showing "cookie not present on callback" and token validation path that clears session. here's the token validation error we logged:
```
ERROR idp.callback: token validation failed: missing_claim azp for client-type public
```
we should avoid bouncing users to login after successful idp exchange; instead detect idp success and surface explicit error that points to cookie issues.

julia_sre: agreed. change UX to show a specific message "Session cookie blocked by browser. Try clearing cookies or using a private window" rather than generic redirect. create a follow-up story.

alex_support: Acme replied they tried incognito and it worked — so workaround validated. sending them ETA and will keep them updated. :thumbsup:

sam_security: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/webapp/pull/1245 — sets SameSite=None; Secure; HttpOnly for callback path and adds feature-flag.

ida_idp: after canary, i'll run the cross-site POST smoke test and monitor idp logs for success for the customer session id.

julia_sre: good. logging actions and next steps in INC-2026-045. keep me posted on canary health.

alex_support: thanks all, i'll close this thread once prod patch is live and customer confirms. :white_check_mark:
